S03 student guide: Gateways

Goal

Today you will route requests by type, by decision, and notify one or more people.

Before class

Start Camunda with Iniciar Camunda, then go down the table in order.

Open Link What to do
The end-of-session check, for your own computer https://sigifredolaengle.github.io/camunda-12-sessions/s03/class-s03.zip Only on your own computer, before anything else: unzip it and double-click desplegar-clase.bat (macOS: desplegar-clase.command). In the lab, Iniciar Camunda has already deployed it.
Tasklist http://127.0.0.1:8080/tasklist Complete the tasks of your instances. User and password: demo / demo.
Operate http://localhost:8080/operate Look at instances, tokens, variables and incidents. User and password: demo / demo.
Your model from session 2 your thread-s02.bpmn Open it in the Modeler: step 3 starts from it.
If you do not have it thread-s02.bpmn, request-intake.form, review-request-s02.form Download the three. Deploy the two forms first, then the model.
Tasklist, tab Processes http://127.0.0.1:8080/tasklist/processes At the end (step 7): start S03 · End-of-session check.

How to work today

  • Steps 1 and 2 are on the projector: watch, and answer the teacher’s questions. You do not deploy Hardware retailer.
  • Steps 3 to 6 are yours: work with this guide and the Modeler side by side, and keep Operate and Tasklist open in two tabs.
  • Step 7: the engine checks your work and sends the result to the teacher.

Before you start an instance: check the data. Every time you deploy and start instances, look at the model and follow the path the instance will take. For each variable: is it read on that path, and will it have a value of the right type by then, from the start of the instance, a form or a script task? Missing data gives an incident, or an empty result (null) without any warning. Where there is a table, tick the variables you checked; not required means that the path does not need it, and result that the path produces it: look at its value in Operate at the end. Variable numbers (#) do not change from table to table: one series for Hardware retailer (steps 1 and 2) and another for the running case (steps 3 to 6). The ticks are only for you: reloading the page clears them.

Two kinds of code in this guide.

  • A grey block with a Copy button is data: copy and paste it.
  • A block marked Type it yourself is what you are learning today. Type it in the Modeler, character by character: that is how you learn where the quotes, the equals sign and the parentheses go.

FEEL expressions are written here without the leading equals sign. In the Modeler every expression starts with it.

Step 1: the worked example, tokens

On the projector; you do not deploy Hardware retailer. The teacher plays the OMG Hardware retailer first with the token simulation and then on the engine, and you follow the tokens in the figure.

1.1 The token simulation: every path

The teacher switches on Token Simulation in the Modeler. At each exclusive or inclusive gateway the simulation asks which branch to take. Follow the figure and find every path an order can take:

Path Mode of delivery extra insurance required Tasks of the branch of Clerk
1 normal post no Check if extra insurance is necessary, Fill in a post label
2 normal post yes Check if extra insurance is necessary, then Fill in a post label and Take out extra insurance at the same time
3 special carrier does not apply Request quotes from carriers, Assign a carrier & prepare paperwork

In all three, Package goods runs at the same time as the branch of Clerk, and Add paperwork and move package to pick area waits for both.

1.2 The same cases on the engine: A-1 and A-2

The teacher deploys the model (the figure above) and, before starting, the class checks the data of the two instances:

# Variable Read in Comes from A-1 A-2
1 orderId nobody: only shown in forms start not required not required
2 weightKg nobody: only shown in forms start not required not required
3 orderValue nobody: only shown in forms start not required not required
4 deliveryMode arrow special carrier task Decide if normal post or special shipment
5 insuranceRequired arrow extra insurance required task Check if extra insurance is necessary not required

The teacher starts the two instances from the Modeler (play icon) and follows them in Operate and Tasklist:

  • A-1 takes path 2: normal post with extra insurance required. Package goods is completed first, and its token waits at the parallel join.
  • A-2 takes path 3: special carrier. Take out extra insurance never starts and nothing waits for it.

The data the teacher starts the two cases with (you do not need to run them):

{"orderId": "A-1", "weightKg": 5, "orderValue": 800}
{"orderId": "A-2", "weightKg": 5, "orderValue": 800}

1.3 Think about

  1. After the gateway that follows Goods to ship, how many tokens are there?
  2. With normal post and extra insurance required, which two tasks appear at the same time?
  3. What does the gateway after those two tasks wait for?
  4. Why is the merge of the two delivery modes an exclusive gateway and not a parallel one?
  5. Does the engine do the same as the simulation?

Step 2: the data of the process, and what goes wrong

On the projector. The data below is what the teacher uses; you do not need to run it. These are the variables of the process:

# Variable Type Set or changed in Form
1 orderId string start of the instance shown in decide-delivery and check-insurance
2 weightKg number start of the instance shown in decide-delivery
3 orderValue number start of the instance shown in decide-delivery and check-insurance
4 deliveryMode string: "post" or "special" task Decide if normal post or special shipment decide-delivery (radio)
5 insuranceRequired boolean: false if nobody ticks it task Check if extra insurance is necessary check-insurance (checkbox)

The conditions read those variables: deliveryMode = "special" on the arrow special carrier (normal post is the default flow), and insuranceRequired = true on the arrow extra insurance required.

2.1 One more rule, and three instances

The teacher deploys a version of Hardware retailer with one more rule: Take out extra insurance also when orderValue is over 1000. The arrow extra insurance required becomes extra insurance required or value over 1000, with the condition insuranceRequired = true or orderValue > 1000.

Before starting, the class checks the data of the three instances below (in the three, deliveryMode = "post"). Which one does not pass?

# Variable Read in Comes from B-1 B-2 B-3
1 orderId nobody: only shown in forms start not required not required not required
2 weightKg nobody: only shown in forms start not required not required not required
3 orderValue arrow extra insurance required or value over 1000 start
4 deliveryMode arrow special carrier task Decide if normal post or special shipment
5 insuranceRequired arrow extra insurance required or value over 1000 task Check if extra insurance is necessary

Then the teacher starts them. In the three, Decide if normal post or special shipment → deliveryMode = "post" and Check if extra insurance is necessary → insuranceRequired = false (box not ticked).

B-1, orderValue = 800: only Fill in a post label.

{"orderId": "B-1", "weightKg": 5, "orderValue": 800}

B-2, orderValue = 1500: Fill in a post label and Take out extra insurance, because of the value rule.

{"orderId": "B-2", "weightKg": 5, "orderValue": 1500}

B-3, without orderValue: it stops at the inclusive gateway with an incident.

{"orderId": "B-3", "weightKg": 5}

2.2 Repairing B-3 in Operate

B-3 stopped because orderValue > 1000 with no orderValue is neither true nor false. In Operate, tab Variables, the teacher uses Add Variable: orderValue = 900. Then tab Incidents, Retry Incident: the instance goes on from the gateway, with only Fill in a post label.

2.3 A value of the wrong type: B-5

The check also looks at the type. B-5 starts with orderValue = "1500", as text. Text and a number cannot be compared: the same incident. The repair: edit orderValue (pencil icon) to the number 1500, then Retry Incident. The instance takes the arrow extra insurance required or value over 1000.

{"orderId": "B-5", "weightKg": 5, "orderValue": "1500"}

2.4 Rules for safe conditions

  • Compare with a single equals sign: insuranceRequired = true is false, not an error, when the variable does not exist.
  • Guard an ordering comparison, so that a missing value gives false: amount != null and amount > 100.
  • Give each variable the right type: 1500, not "1500".
  • Always give an exclusive gateway a default flow. Without it, if no condition is true, the instance stops with an incident (you will do this in step 6).

2.5 Think about

  1. Which variables come from the start of the instance, and which from a form?
  2. Why did B-2 take the arrow extra insurance required or value over 1000, if insuranceRequired = false?
  3. Why did B-3 stop, and why did B-1 not?
  4. Why is "1500" not the same as 1500 for the engine?
  5. After Retry, does the instance start again from the beginning?

Step 3: route by type and decide

Now you work on the running case. First the problem, on paper; then the model.

The problem. A student sends a request: a certificate of enrolment, the postponement of an exam, or the recognition of a course. The certificate is issued at once. Any other request is reviewed by a person, who approves or rejects it: an approved request is registered; for a rejected one, a letter is prepared. At the end, the student is always informed; the instructor too, if it is a postponement; and the registrar, if it is a recognition that was approved.

The paths. Each request follows exactly one row. The decision does not exist at the beginning: a person gives it in Review request. That is why the model asks twice, with two exclusive gateways: first Type of request?, and later, only for some requests, Approved?.

Case requestType decision Arrows Tasks Result Built in Run in
C1 "certificate" not needed certificate Issue certificate certificateNumber 3.1 3.1, 3.3, step 5
C2 any other "approved" needs review, approved Review request, Register decision registered 3.1, 3.2 4.3, step 5
C3 any other any other needs review, rejected Review request, Prepare rejection letter letter 3.1, 3.2 3.2, step 5, step 6

Where the table says any other, the model has a default flow.

The notifications. Here one or more rows hold for the same request: an inclusive gateway.

Rule requestType decision Arrow Task Result Built in Run in
N1 any any, or none always Notify student studentMessage 4.1, 4.2 4.3, step 5
N2 "postponement" any postponement Notify instructor instructorMessage 4.1, 4.2 step 5
N3 "recognition" "approved" recognition approved Notify registrar registrarMessage 4.1, 4.2 4.3

Before you model.

  • Deploy the two forms of session 2, request-intake.form and review-request-s02.form (form id review-request): the engine in the lab starts empty, and without the second one Review request stops with an incident.
  • Open your thread-s02.bpmn and save it as thread-s03.bpmn. Keep the process id student-request. This is where you start:

  • Delete the script task Build summary: from today the result depends on the path. Review request goes straight to Request closed; if the arrow disappeared, draw it. Every model you deploy today is complete: all its paths reach Request closed.

These are the variables of this step:

# Variable Type Set in Form
1 requestType string: "certificate", "postponement" or "recognition" start of the instance request-intake (select)
2 studentId string start of the instance request-intake (text)
3 studentName string start of the instance request-intake (text)
4 studentEmail string start of the instance request-intake (text)
5 course string start of the instance request-intake (text)
6 days number, for requestType = "postponement" start of the instance request-intake (number)
7 reason string, optional start of the instance request-intake (text area)
8 dueDate string (a date) script task Compute due date none
9 certificateNumber string script task Issue certificate none
10 decision string: "approved" or "rejected" task Review request review-request (radio)
11 comment string, optional task Review request review-request (text area)
12 registered boolean script task Register decision none
13 letter string script task Prepare rejection letter none

3.1 Route by type

You build C1, and the beginning of C2 and C3: the arrow needs review.

  1. After Compute due date, add an exclusive gateway Type of request?.
  2. Draw an arrow from it to a new script task Issue certificate. Name the arrow certificate, select it (the arrow, not the diamond) and set its condition:
requestType = "certificate"
  1. Issue certificate is a script task (FEEL expression) with result variable certificateNumber:
"CERT-" + studentId + "-" + string(today())
  1. The arrow needs review goes to Review request. Mark it as default flow (wrench icon on the arrow).
  2. Connect Issue certificate to Request closed. Review request already goes there.

Your model should now look like this:

Deploy and try. Deploy. Before you start an instance with requestType = "certificate", check its data in the model:

# Variable Read in Comes from Checked?
1 requestType arrow certificate; form review-request start
2 studentId task Issue certificate; form review-request start
3 studentName form review-request start not required
4 studentEmail form review-request start not required
5 course form review-request start not required
6 days form review-request start not required
7 reason form review-request start not required
8 dueDate form review-request task Compute due date result
9 certificateNumber nobody task Issue certificate result
10 decision nobody yet (3.2) task Review request not required
11 comment nobody yet (3.2) task Review request not required

Start it from the Modeler (play icon). It takes the arrow certificate and completes with certificateNumber.

{"studentName": "Ana Rojas", "studentId": "19.876.543-0", "studentEmail": "ana@example.org", "requestType": "certificate", "course": "BPM"}

3.2 Decide

You build the rest of C2 and C3.

  1. After Review request, add an exclusive gateway Approved?.
  2. Arrow approved to a script task Register decision (expression true, result variable registered). No condition reads registered: it only leaves a record of the approval. The condition of the arrow:
decision = "approved"
  1. Arrow rejected, marked default flow, to a script task Prepare rejection letter, result variable letter. The parentheses around the if are required: without them the model does not deploy.
"Dear " + studentName + ", your request was rejected. " + (if comment = null then "" else comment)
  1. Connect Register decision and Prepare rejection letter to Request closed. Review request now goes only to Approved?: if its old arrow to Request closed is still there, delete it.

Your model should now look like this:

Deploy and try. Deploy. You run C3; C2 comes in 4.3. Before you start an instance with requestType = "recognition" and, in Tasklist, decision = "rejected", check its data in the model. comment is not required: the if of the letter takes care of an empty one.

# Variable Read in Comes from Checked?
1 requestType arrow certificate; form review-request start
2 studentId task Issue certificate; form review-request start not required
3 studentName task Prepare rejection letter; form review-request start
4 studentEmail form review-request start not required
5 course form review-request start not required
6 days form review-request start not required
7 reason form review-request start not required
8 dueDate form review-request task Compute due date result
9 certificateNumber nobody task Issue certificate not required
10 decision arrow approved task Review request
11 comment task Prepare rejection letter task Review request not required
12 registered nobody task Register decision not required
13 letter nobody task Prepare rejection letter result

Start it from the Modeler (play icon) and complete Review request in Tasklist with decision = "rejected": it completes with letter.

{"studentName": "Ana Rojas", "studentId": "19.876.543-0", "studentEmail": "ana@example.org", "requestType": "recognition", "course": "BPM"}

3.3 Merge, deploy and try

You join C1, C2 and C3. An end event accepts several arrows, so 3.2 runs without a merge. From step 4 something else follows the three paths, so they need one first.

  1. Take the three arrows to Request closed (from Issue certificate, Register decision and Prepare rejection letter) to one more exclusive gateway, and draw one arrow from it to Request closed.
  2. Your model should now look like this:

  1. Deploy. You run C1 again. Its data are those of 3.1: the path reads the same variables, and registered and letter are not required.
  2. Start it from the Modeler (play icon): as in 3.1, but now it passes the merge.
{"studentName": "Ana Rojas", "studentId": "19.876.543-0", "studentEmail": "ana@example.org", "requestType": "certificate", "course": "BPM"}

In Operate, look at the path and the variables. The instances of 3.1 to 3.3, and later the one of 4.3, are only a first test: the instances of step 5 are the ones that count for the check.

3.4 Think about

  1. Why does the arrow needs review deploy without a condition?
  2. Which path would a request with requestType = "exam" take?
  3. Why is the merge an exclusive gateway and not a parallel one?
  4. Which of the variables that a task sets (8 to 13) do not exist at the end of the instance with requestType = "certificate"?
  5. Why does the if of the letter need parentheses?

Step 4: notifications

After the three paths merge, the process informs the people concerned: the rules N1, N2 and N3 of step 3. This is where you start (the model of 3.3):

These are the variables that the notifications read or set:

# Variable Type Set in Form
1 requestType string: "certificate", "postponement" or "recognition" start of the instance request-intake (select)
2 studentId string start of the instance request-intake (text)
3 studentName string start of the instance request-intake (text)
4 studentEmail string start of the instance request-intake (text)
5 course string start of the instance request-intake (text)
10 decision string: "approved" or "rejected" task Review request review-request (radio)
14 studentMessage string script task Notify student none
15 instructorMessage string script task Notify instructor none
16 registrarMessage string script task Notify registrar none

4.1 Who must be informed?

  1. Delete the arrow from the merge to Request closed. After the merge, add an inclusive gateway Who must be informed? with three arrows, each to a new script task:
Rule Arrow Script task
N1 always Notify student
N2 postponement Notify instructor
N3 recognition approved Notify registrar
  1. Set the conditions of the three arrows, in the same order:
true
requestType = "postponement"
requestType = "recognition" and decision = "approved"

4.2 The three notifications

  1. Each script task (FEEL expression) has its result variable:
Script task # Result variable
Notify student 14 studentMessage
Notify instructor 15 instructorMessage
Notify registrar 16 registrarMessage
  1. The expressions of the three tasks, in the same order:
"To " + studentEmail + ": your " + requestType + " request was processed."
"Instructor of " + course + ": postponement request of " + studentName
"Registrar: recognise " + course + " for " + studentId

4.3 Join, deploy and try

  1. Join the three tasks with another inclusive gateway, and connect it to Request closed.
  2. Your model should now look like this:

  1. Deploy. You run C2 with N1 and N3. Before you start an instance with requestType = "recognition" and, in Tasklist, decision = "approved", check its data in the model:
# Variable Read in Comes from Checked?
1 requestType arrows certificate, postponement and recognition approved; task Notify student; form review-request start
2 studentId tasks Issue certificate and Notify registrar; form review-request start
3 studentName tasks Prepare rejection letter and Notify instructor; form review-request start not required
4 studentEmail task Notify student; form review-request start
5 course tasks Notify instructor and Notify registrar; form review-request start
6 days form review-request start not required
7 reason form review-request start not required
8 dueDate form review-request task Compute due date result
9 certificateNumber nobody task Issue certificate not required
10 decision arrows approved and recognition approved task Review request
11 comment task Prepare rejection letter task Review request not required
12 registered nobody task Register decision result
13 letter nobody task Prepare rejection letter not required
14 studentMessage nobody task Notify student result
15 instructorMessage nobody task Notify instructor not required
16 registrarMessage nobody task Notify registrar result
  1. Start it from the Modeler (play icon) and complete Review request in Tasklist with decision = "approved". It passes Notify student and Notify registrar.
{"studentName": "Ana Rojas", "studentId": "19.876.543-0", "studentEmail": "ana@example.org", "requestType": "recognition", "course": "BPM"}

In Operate, look at the path: the inclusive join waited for two branches, not three.

4.4 Think about

  1. In this instance, how many tokens leave Who must be informed?
  2. What would happen if the join were a parallel gateway?
  3. And if it were an exclusive gateway?
  4. What is the arrow always for?
  5. With requestType = "postponement" and decision = "rejected", does the instance pass Notify instructor? Should it be so?

The three instances of this step are the ones that count for the check of step 7. Start them with the version that you deployed in 4.3: those of steps 3.1 to 3.3 have no studentMessage.

5.1 Check the data

5.4 Think about

  2. Instance 1 has no decision. Why does the condition of recognition approved not give an incident?
  3. What would happen with requestType = "Postponement", with a capital letter?
  4. Which instance of today passed Notify registrar, the path that is missing here?
  5. Combine the two tables of step 3: how many different requests are there, and which one did nobody run today?

Step 6: break it and repair it

You start from the model of 4.3 and break it in two ways: one error shows when you deploy, the other only when an instance runs. Then you repair it.

6.1 An error when you deploy

  1. In Approved?, select the arrow rejected, wrench icon, Sequence flow: it is no longer the default flow.
  2. Deploy. The engine refuses: Must have a condition or be default flow. There is no new version: the one of 4.3 is still the latest.

6.2 An incident when you run

  1. Delete the arrow rejected: C3 loses its path. Leave Prepare rejection letter and its arrow to the merge alone. Your model should now look like this:

  1. Deploy: this time the engine accepts it. Before you start an instance with requestType = "recognition" and, in Tasklist, decision = "rejected", check its data in the model. Follow the path as far as it goes:
# Variable Read in Comes from Checked?
1 requestType arrows certificate, postponement and recognition approved; task Notify student; form review-request start
2 studentId tasks Issue certificate and Notify registrar; form review-request start not required
3 studentName tasks Prepare rejection letter and Notify instructor; form review-request start not required
4 studentEmail task Notify student; form review-request start not required
5 course tasks Notify instructor and Notify registrar; form review-request start not required
6 days form review-request start not required
7 reason form review-request start not required
8 dueDate form review-request task Compute due date result
9 certificateNumber nobody task Issue certificate not required
10 decision arrow approved (and, further on, recognition approved) task Review request
11 comment task Prepare rejection letter task Review request not required
12 registered nobody task Register decision not required
13 letter nobody task Prepare rejection letter not required
14 studentMessage nobody task Notify student not required
15 instructorMessage nobody task Notify instructor not required
16 registrarMessage nobody task Notify registrar not required
  1. The data are all there. Start it from the Modeler (play icon) and complete Review request in Tasklist with decision = "rejected".
{"studentName": "Ana Rojas", "studentId": "19.876.543-0", "studentEmail": "ana@example.org", "requestType": "recognition", "course": "BPM"}
  1. In Operate, the instance stopped at Approved? with the incident CONDITION_ERROR: Expected at least one condition to evaluate to true, or to have a default flow.

6.3 Does Retry repair it?

In step 2, Retry Incident was enough after changing a variable. Before you try, tick what you expect:

  • the instance goes on;
  • the incident comes back.

Then, in Operate, tab Incidents, Retry Incident. Wait a few seconds and look again.

6.4 Repair

  1. Put the arrow rejected back, from Approved? to Prepare rejection letter, name it and mark it default flow. Your model should look like the one of 4.3 again:

  1. Deploy. A new version does not move the stopped instance: in Operate, cancel it (Cancel instance).
  2. Start a new one, with the same data (its check is the column of instance 3 in 5.1), and complete Review request with decision = "rejected". It completes, with letter and studentMessage.
{"studentName": "Ana Rojas", "studentId": "19.876.543-0", "studentEmail": "ana@example.org", "requestType": "recognition", "course": "BPM"}

6.5 Think about

  1. Why does an instance with decision = "approved" complete in the broken model, and one with decision = "rejected" not?
  2. Why was Retry enough for B-3, and not here?
  3. Is Retry enough after deploying the repaired model?
  4. What would happen if, in Operate, you changed decision to "approved" and then pressed Retry? Is it a repair?

Step 7: the end-of-session check

The engine reads what steps 3 to 6 left behind: your latest student-request, your three instances and the incident of step 6. This check is your lab for today.

7.1 Before you start

Tick what is ready:

  • the latest version of student-request is the repaired model of 6.4, deployed some seconds ago;
  • the three instances of 5.2 are completed in Operate;
  • no instance of student-request is stopped at an incident.

7.2 Run the check

  1. In Tasklist, tab Processes: S03 · End-of-session check → Start process (Iniciar proceso).
  2. Fill in your RUT (format 12.345.678-5, with the right check digit), names and e-mail.
  3. Open the task S03 · Check your work and complete it.

If something is missing, the task comes back with Feedback. If everything is there, it does not come back.

7.3 If something is missing

The feedback names the step of this guide. Fix it, wait a few seconds if you deployed, and complete the task again.

The feedback is about Go to What to do
no deployed version 4.3 or 6.4 deploy thread-s03.bpmn; the process id is student-request
exclusive gateways 3.1 to 3.3 there are three: Type of request?, Approved? and the merge
default flows 3.1, 3.2, 6.4 mark needs review and rejected as default flow
certificateNumber, registered or letter 3.1, 3.2 write the result variable in its script task
inclusive or parallel gateways 4.1, 4.3 Who must be informed? and the join before Request closed are inclusive; there is no parallel gateway
studentMessage, instructorMessage or registrarMessage 4.2 write the result variable in its script task
an instance that is not completed 5.2 start that instance again with the latest version, and finish it in Tasklist
no condition incident 6.2 make the incident: the check needs to see it
an instance still stopped 6.4 cancel it in Operate

7.4 How to know that you finished

  1. In Operate, among the finished instances, the one of S03 · End-of-session check is completed and reached Check completed: your result is in the teacher’s sheet.
  2. If instead Tasklist shows the task S03 · Results not sent: tell the teacher, your result did not arrive. Tell the teacher. If your RUT has a mistake, complete that task and start the check again with the right one.

7.5 Think about
